text:
amy_sales: Hey team — Acme buyer (Carla) pinged about the POC checklist. They want our completed SIG/CAIQ + answers, plus clarity on DPA deletion timelines and who signs SCCs. Can we confirm who's owning the vendor questionnaire and what the deletion SLA is for hosted vs dedicated/private?

mike_se: I can own the tech-side SIG/CAIQ responses. Quick summary for POC: hosted API (default) — request logs and full prompt/response payloads are retained for 30 days for debugging and abuse detection; embeddings & model artifacts are not persisted beyond cache TTLs. Dedicated customers can opt into no-log mode and we support BYOK (KMS) for at-rest keys. Private (VPC/on-prem) — customer controls retention entirely.

carla_customer: Thanks Mike. For DSARs, what’s the workflow? If an end-user requests deletion, do you need our team to file through Redwood or can we trigger deletions programmatically?

mike_se: You can do both. For hosted we provide: 1) programmatic bulk deletion endpoint (example below), 2) support ticket for legal/audit ops if you need certified deletion proof. Example curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/customers/ACME123/data-delete \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \\n  -d '{"scope":"prompts_and_responses","since":"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"}'
```
Note: deletion triggers background job; typical completion time depends on volume — hosted SLA target is 72 hours, backups purged within 90 days unless you have a private/dedicated config.

nora_security: Adding security context: we'll deliver a populated CAIQ file and SOC2 Type II summary. On deletion semantics: for hosted customers we treat prompts/outputs as customer data and scope deletions accordingly; however logs and telemetry (anonymized metrics) are stored aggregated for platform monitoring and aren't tied to PII. For customers who require shorter retention we recommend Dedicated with log-disable + BYOK. Also we maintain an access log and can export audit trails for DSAR evidence.

oliver_legal: From the legal/DPA side we're seeing two recurring redline asks from enterprise buyers: (1) stricter backup retention caps (they want <=30 days), and (2) subprocessors list + 30 days notice before adding new subprocessors. We typically accept 90-day backup purge and 30-day subprocessors notice; if Acme insists on 30-day backups we can escalate to Enterprise legal for a carve-out tied to a Dedicated pricing uplift. Who wants to pick up negotiation?

amy_sales: I'll take the negotiation with Acme and loop in legal — Oliver, can you draft suggested clause language that preserves our platform reliability wording? Need something we can hand to their counsel.

oliver_legal: Sure — will draft a narrow amendment: specify primary deletion SLA (72 hours), backup purge window (90 days) with option for expedited purge for Dedicated deployments; subprocessors notice 30 days, plus written consent for changes that materially affect data residency. Sending initial redline later today. :memo:

jana_eng: Quick technical note the security team should confirm in CAIQ: KV cache used for inference lives in GPU memory and is not written to disk; core model weights are read-only; any explicit customer artifacts (uploads, fine-tuning datasets) are stored in encrypted object storage with per-tenant prefixes. For the POC we should provide a diagram of dataflow (I can sketch one).

vendor-risk-bot: Vendor-risk ticket VRT-2024-112 created for Acme POC — questionnaire requested, deadline 2024-05-02. Assigned: nora_security, mike_se.

carla_customer: Appreciate the transparency. Two final asks from our side: (A) can you provide signed SCCs or the EU SCC Annex paperwork (we're in EU) and (B) can you confirm whether Redwood ever uses customer prompts to train models?

mike_se: (A) We support SCCs — Operations/Legal will produce executed docs once contract is in place. (B) No — for Hosted customers we do not use customer prompts/outputs to train public models. We may use aggregated telemetry for quality-of-service improvements but that's explicitly excluded in the DPA; customers can opt-out of even aggregated telemetry under Dedicated/Private.

nora_security: I'll attach the CAIQ + SOC2 excerpts and a mapped control matrix linking CAIQ questions to our SOC2 and internal policies. Also adding a short note about BYOK flow for KMS and HSM integration for Private deployments.

amy_sales: Great — plan: Mike and Nora deliver SIG/CAIQ answers and diagram by EOD, Oliver sends DPA redline language, and I'll run pricing impact for Dedicated carve-out. Carla — we'll share a consolidated packet within 24 hours and set a call to walk through. :phone: 

carla_customer: Perfect. Looking forward to the packet and the walkthrough.

amy_sales: 👍 thanks everyone — tagging follow-ups: @nora_security please post CAIQ link here when ready; @oliver_legal please paste the redline snippet so we can share with Acme counsel.
